# Octo Browser API

> Octo Browser provides a comprehensive API for browser profile automation, enabling programmatic control of browser profiles, fingerprints, proxies, team members, and the local desktop client.

The cloud API uses RESTful principles with JSON request/response bodies. All cloud requests authenticate via the `X-Octo-Api-Token` header (each named token carries its own permissions) against `https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation`. The local client API runs on `http://localhost:58888` (configurable via `OCTO_LOCAL_PORT`) inside the desktop app and is unauthenticated.

Important notes:
- Authentication: send `X-Octo-Api-Token: <token>` for every cloud request. A token without the required permission gets `403` with code `no_permission`.
- Standard envelope: `{ "success": bool, "msg": string, "data": ..., "code": string | null }`. Paginated listings (profiles, trash bin, fingerprint renderers, provider proxies) add `total_count` and `page`; teams subaccounts/invites add only `total_count`; other listings return a bare `data` array.
- Validation errors return HTTP 400 with `{"validation_error": {"body_params" | "query_params" | "path_params": [...]}}`.
- Pagination: `page` is zero-based; `page_len` is one of `10, 25, 50, 100`.
- Rate limits: 50–1000 RPM and 500–50000 RPH depending on subscription, shared by all API tokens of the team and with local-client profile operations; failed requests (400/409/422) cost extra points. Honour `Retry-After` and `X-Ratelimit-*` headers.
- Resource UUIDs are 32-character hex strings; team extension IDs use `<extension-id>@<version>`; tags and folders are referenced by name in profile payloads.
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC without a timezone suffix; prices and balances are decimal strings.
- Machine-readable spec: [openapi.json](openapi.json) (OpenAPI 3.0, covers the cloud API including endpoints absent from the official spec).
- Mirror hosts: `app.octobrowser-mirror1.com` / `.net` / `.org`.

## Getting Started

- [Authentication](api/authentication.md): Named API tokens, per-token permissions, mirror endpoints.
- [Rate Limiting](api/rate-limiting.md): RPM/RPH budgets, headers, and 429 handling.
- [Error Handling](api/errors.md): Business and validation error envelopes, error code reference.

## Core Resources

- [Profiles](api/profiles.md): Create, update, list, force-stop, transfer, export, import, and password-protect browser profiles; trash bin and restore (17 endpoints).
- [Tags](api/tags.md): Manage coloured profile tags (4 endpoints).
- [Folders](api/folders.md): Group profiles into folders, introduced in Octo 3.0 (4 endpoints).
- [Proxies](api/proxies.md): Manage saved HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS/SSH and WireGuard/AmneziaWG VPN proxies and reference them from profiles (4 endpoints).
- [Proxy Providers](api/proxy-providers.md): Proxy Shop — list providers, look up countries/regions/cities/ISPs, list, buy, rename, and delete provider proxies (11 endpoints).
- [Teams](api/teams.md): Manage subaccounts, invitations, team-installed extensions, and read subscription/plan usage (9 endpoints).
- [Action Log](api/action-log.md): Real-time team audit stream over WebSocket (`wss://.../ws/action_log`) with watermark-based resume (1 WebSocket endpoint).
- [Fingerprint](api/fingerprint.md): Browser fingerprint object plus lookup endpoints for platforms, renderers, screens, and mobile device models (4 endpoints).

## Optional

- [Local Client API](api/local-client.md): Drive the desktop app on `localhost:58888` — start, stop, force_stop, one-time profiles, proxy check, password, auth, and update endpoints (13 endpoints).
- [Docker & Kubernetes](api/docker.md): Run Octo Browser headless inside containers.
- [Automation Libraries](api/automation.md): Selenium, Playwright, Puppeteer/Pyppeteer integration in Node.js, Python, Java, and VB.NET.

# File: api/authentication.md

# Authentication

All cloud API requests require an API token. The local client API on `http://localhost:58888` is **unauthenticated** and intended for use by code running on the same machine. When the desktop client is started with `OCTO_API_TOKEN`, it acts with that token's permissions: local API calls that need a permission the token lacks fail with `no_permission`, and the client's actions appear in the Action Log as `<token name> (API)`.

## Getting Your API Token

API tokens are managed in **Team settings → API tokens** in the Octo Browser desktop app (Base plan or higher). A team can have several **named** tokens, each with its own [permissions](#api-token-permissions):

| Plan     | API tokens |
|----------|------------|
| Base     | 1          |
| Team     | 3          |
| Advanced | 5          |

- The token issued by earlier versions keeps working. It is listed as "API token" with full permissions and counts toward the limit.
- On plans with a single team member, every token has full permissions.
- A token can be regenerated. A desktop client signed in with the old token (via `OCTO_API_TOKEN`) is signed out; update the environment variable and restart the client.

## Using the API Token

Include the token in the `X-Octo-Api-Token` header on every request to `https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/...`:

```bash
curl -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles
```

Every token authenticates the same team workspace, but each token carries its own permissions and may be restricted to certain folders. A call the token is not allowed to make returns `403`:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "msg": "No permission",
  "data": "",
  "code": "no_permission"
}
```

## API Token Permissions

Each token can call only the endpoints its permissions allow. The endpoints below require the listed permission; all paths are relative to `https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation`.

| Permission | Endpoints |
|------------|-----------|
| Create profiles | `POST /profiles`, `POST /profiles/{uuid}/import_cookies`, `POST /profiles/import` (sending `password` on create also needs Profile passwords) |
| Edit profiles | `PATCH /profiles/{uuid}` (without it, `GET /profiles` returns `description` masked as `**`) |
| Delete profiles | `DELETE /profiles`, `GET /profiles/trash_bin`, `POST /profiles/trash_bin/restore` |
| Transfer profiles | `POST /profiles/transfer`, `GET /profiles/export`, `GET /profiles/export/{uuid}`, `POST /profiles/export` |
| Profile passwords | `POST /profiles/set_password`, `POST /profiles/{uuid}/clear_password` |
| Edit tags | `POST /tags`, `PATCH /tags/{uuid}`, `DELETE /tags/{uuid}` |
| Edit folders | `POST /folders`, `PATCH /folders/{uuid}`, `DELETE /folders/{uuid}` (setting `assignable_wo_permission` also needs Manage team) |
| Create proxies | `POST /proxies` |
| Edit proxies | `PATCH /proxies/{uuid}`, `PATCH /proxy_providers/proxies/{uuid}` |
| Delete proxies | `DELETE /proxies/{uuid}`, `DELETE /proxy_providers/proxies/{uuid}` |
| Create paid proxies | `POST /proxy_providers/proxies` |
| Delete extensions | `DELETE /teams/extensions` |
| Manage team | `/teams/subaccounts` and `/teams/invites` (all methods) |
| Action log | `wss://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/ws/action_log` (see [action-log.md](action-log.md)) |

All other endpoints, including read-only lists and lookups (`GET /profiles`, `GET /folders`, `GET /proxies`, `GET /teams/subscription`, …), need no specific permission, but their results are scoped to the token:

- `GET /profiles` returns only profiles visible to the token.
- `GET /folders` returns only folders available to the token (possibly an empty list).
- Passing a `folder` the token cannot access on profile create, update, or import returns `403 no_permission`.

## Alternative Endpoints

If your network blocks the canonical host, the API is also reachable on these mirrors:

- `https://app.octobrowser-mirror1.com`
- `https://app.octobrowser-mirror1.net`
- `https://app.octobrowser-mirror1.org`

The path, headers, and behaviour are identical.

## Environment Variable

Avoid embedding the token in source code. Store it in an environment variable:

```bash
export OCTO_API_TOKEN="your_token_here"
```

The desktop client also reads `OCTO_API_TOKEN` at startup and signs in automatically, which lets you script cold-start automation without `POST /api/auth/login` — see [local-client.md](local-client.md#signing-in-with-an-api-token) for per-OS launch commands.

```python
import os
import requests

headers = {"X-Octo-Api-Token": os.environ["OCTO_API_TOKEN"]}
response = requests.get(
    "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles?page_len=10&page=0",
    headers=headers,
)
```

## Security Notes

- Treat the token like a password. Anyone holding it can act on the team's workspace within the token's permissions.
- Never commit tokens to version control. Add `.env`, secret files, and IDE run-configs to `.gitignore`.
- Rotate tokens periodically from **Team settings → API tokens**, and give each script a token with only the permissions it needs.
- Server-side responses may include cleartext proxy credentials (see [proxies.md](proxies.md)) — log responses carefully.

---

# File: api/rate-limiting.md

# Rate Limiting

The cloud API enforces a Requests-Per-Minute (RPM) and Requests-Per-Hour (RPH) budget. Limits are **shared across the whole team** — calls made with any of the team's API tokens (and by any subaccount) draw from the same bucket. Repeatedly ignoring `429` responses will cause us to enforce stricter limits on the team.

## Limits by Subscription

| Plan      | RPM                          | RPH                                |
|-----------|------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Base      | 50                           | 500                                |
| Team      | 100                          | 1,500                              |
| Advanced  | 200, expandable up to 1,000  | 3,000, expandable up to 50,000     |

For limits beyond 1,000 RPM or 50,000 RPH, contact Octo Browser Technical Support.

## Point Costs of Local Client Operations

Local client API calls (`localhost:58888`) are charged against the same RPM/RPH budget as cloud calls:

| Local operation | Cost |
|-----------------|------|
| `POST /api/profiles/start` | 1 request |
| `POST /api/profiles/stop` | 1 request |
| `POST /api/profiles/password` (set) | 1 request |
| `DELETE /api/profiles/password` | 1 request |
| `POST /api/profiles/force_stop` | 2 requests |
| `POST /api/profiles/one_time/start` | 4 requests |

The following local requests are **not counted** toward the limits: List Active Profiles (`GET /api/profiles/active`), Login, Logout, Get Client Version, Update Client, and Username.

## Cost of Failed Requests

Responses with status `400`, `409` and `422` cost extra rate-limit points. Per the official API FAQ, a `400` costs 6 RPM and 1 RPH. Validate requests before sending them, and fix the request instead of retrying it unchanged.

## Rate Limit Headers

Every cloud API response carries:

```text
Retry-After: 0                   # seconds; 0 means you may send the next request now
X-Ratelimit-Limit: 100           # current RPM limit
X-Ratelimit-Limit-Hour: 1500     # current RPH limit
X-Ratelimit-Remaining: 98        # remaining points this minute
X-Ratelimit-Remaining-Hour: 1460 # remaining points this hour
X-Ratelimit-Reset: 1793102460    # unix timestamp when the minute window resets
```

`X-Ratelimit-Remaining` is the authoritative signal — drop your request rate as it approaches `0`.

Responses also carry the IETF draft `RateLimit` / `RateLimit-Policy` headers (live-verified 2026-11-18):

```text
RateLimit: per_1minute;r=98;t=17, per_1hour;r=1460;t=2057
RateLimit-Policy: per_1minute;q=100;w=60, per_1hour;q=1500;w=3600
```

- `RateLimit`: per window, `r` = remaining points and `t` = seconds until the window resets. The values match `X-Ratelimit-Remaining` / `X-Ratelimit-Remaining-Hour`.
- `RateLimit-Policy`: per window, `q` = quota (limit) and `w` = window length in seconds. The live header can list further policies after these two.

## Reading the Current Budget

[`GET /teams/subscription`](teams.md#get-subscription) returns the current budget in the body, which is handy before starting a large job:

```json
{
  "rate_limits": {
    "rpm": { "limit": 100, "remaining": 98, "reset_at": "2026-10-27T12:01:00" },
    "rph": { "limit": 1500, "remaining": 1460, "reset_at": "2026-10-27T12:35:00" }
  }
}
```

`remaining` already counts this request. `reset_at` is ISO 8601 in **UTC** without a timezone suffix (like all timestamps in response bodies); `rpm.reset_at` equals `X-Ratelimit-Reset` converted to UTC.

## Handling 429 Responses

When the bucket is empty, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a non-zero `Retry-After` header. Because the budget is team-wide, **stop all requests across the team** (not just the one that got the `429`) and pause for `Retry-After` seconds before retrying. Ignoring `429` responses may lead to stricter limits being enforced on the team.

```python
import time
import requests

def request_with_retry(method, url, headers, **kwargs):
    while True:
        response = requests.request(method, url, headers=headers, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code != 429:
            return response
        retry_after = int(response.headers.get("Retry-After", "1"))
        time.sleep(max(retry_after, 1))
```

## Best Practices

1. **Watch the headers.** Slow down before you hit `0` rather than after.
2. **Linear pacing beats bursts.** Spread heavy jobs evenly across the minute.
3. **Cache lookups.** Don't call `GET /tags`, `GET /proxies`, or `GET /fingerprint/renderers` on every iteration.
4. **One-time profiles cost 4×.** When scraping at volume, batch with saved profiles where possible.
5. **Local client calls count too.** Profile start/stop/password operations on `localhost:58888` draw from the same team budget (see the point-cost table above); only the read-only client endpoints are free.
6. **Don't retry failed requests blindly.** `400`/`409`/`422` responses cost extra points; fix the request first.

# File: api/errors.md

# Error Handling

The cloud API uses two distinct error envelopes: a **business error envelope** (returned for most non-2xx responses, including auth failures, missing resources, and conflicts) and a **validation envelope** (returned when the request body, query string, or path parameters are malformed).

Data types in response bodies: dates are ISO 8601 in **UTC** without a timezone suffix (`"2026-10-27T12:00:00"`); prices and balances are decimal strings (`"125.5"`, `"12.5"`).

## Business Error Envelope

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "msg": "Human-readable message",
  "code": "machine_readable_code",
  "data": ""
}
```

- `success` is always `false` on errors.
- `code` is a stable identifier you can branch on. The list below is not exhaustive.
- `data` is `""` for most errors and an object for partial-failure responses (e.g. mass `force_stop`, `DELETE /profiles` with nothing deleted, `POST /profiles/trash_bin/restore` with nothing restored).

Real samples:

```http
HTTP/2 401
{"success":false,"msg":"Invalid or missing API token.","data":"","code":"api_token"}
```

```http
HTTP/2 403
{"success":false,"msg":"No permission","data":"","code":"no_permission"}
```

```http
HTTP/2 404
{"success":false,"msg":"Cannot find profile by uuid","data":"","code":"not_found"}
```

```http
HTTP/2 404
{"success":false,"msg":"Profiles not found or active","data":{"deleted_uuids":[],"active_uuids":[],"protected_uuids":[],"not_found_uuids":["a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90"]},"code":"not_found"}
```

The last sample is `DELETE /profiles` when nothing was deleted: unlike most errors, `data` carries the result lists.

Some semantic validation errors also use the business envelope, with `code` set to `"validation_error"` (distinct from the `{"validation_error": {…}}` object below). Example — creating a `mac` profile with an `os_version` the platform does not allow:

```http
HTTP/2 400
{"success":false,"msg":"OS version does not match allowed versions for the platform","data":"","code":"validation_error"}
```

## Validation Envelope

Bad query parameters, body fields, or path parameters return HTTP 400 with a different shape (no `success`/`msg`/`code` fields):

```json
{
  "validation_error": {
    "query_params": [
      {
        "type": "enum",
        "loc": ["page_len"],
        "msg": "Input should be 10, 25, 50 or 100",
        "input": "1"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The key says where the invalid field is: `query_params`, `body_params`, or `path_params`. Body validation example:

```json
{
  "validation_error": {
    "body_params": [
      { "type": "string_too_long", "loc": ["name"], "msg": "String should have at most 20 characters", "input": "this-name-is-way-too-long" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Path validation example (unknown proxy `kind` in a provider lookup URL):

```json
{
  "validation_error": {
    "path_params": [
      { "type": "enum", "loc": ["kind"], "msg": "Input should be 'mobile', 'residential' or 'data_center'", "input": "bogus" }
    ]
  }
}
```

When you receive a 400, check whether `validation_error` is an **object** (validation envelope). Otherwise parse the response as a business error — its `code` may itself be the string `"validation_error"`.

## HTTP Status Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 200  | OK |
| 201  | Created — returned by `POST /profiles`, `POST /tags`, and `POST /proxies` (`POST /folders` returns 200). |
| 207  | Multi-Status — declared by the official OpenAPI spec for partial results of `POST /profiles/import`, `POST /profiles/export`, `POST /profiles/trash_bin/restore` and mass `POST /profiles/force_stop` (the Postman collection also documents it for mass force-stop). Not live-verified. |
| 400  | Bad request — body, query or path failed validation, or a domain rule rejected the call. Costs extra rate-limit points (see [rate-limiting.md](rate-limiting.md#cost-of-failed-requests)). |
| 401  | Invalid or missing `X-Octo-Api-Token`. |
| 403  | The token lacks the required permission (`no_permission`), the profile/folder is not available to the token, a plan limit was reached, or the API is disabled for the subscription. |
| 404  | Resource (profile, tag, proxy, subaccount, …) does not exist. |
| 409  | Conflict — resource is locked, running, or in a state that forbids the operation. Costs extra rate-limit points. |
| 415  | Unsupported Media Type — a request body was sent with a non-JSON `Content-Type` (per the official Postman collection). |
| 422  | Not used by the cloud API: validation failures are `400` with the `validation_error` envelope above, and the current official OpenAPI spec no longer declares 422 (older versions did). The **local client** API does return `422` with `{ "detail": [{ "loc": [...], "msg": "...", "type": "..." }] }` — see [local-client.md](local-client.md#error-responses). |
| 429  | Rate limit exceeded; see [rate-limiting.md](rate-limiting.md). |
| 5xx  | Server-side issue. Retry with exponential backoff. |

## Error Code Reference

The `code` field on the business error envelope. Codes prefixed with a domain (`profiles.`, `tags.`, …) are scoped to that resource.

### General

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `api_token`         | Invalid or missing `X-Octo-Api-Token`. |
| `not_found`         | Resource UUID does not exist (also returned for an unknown or temporary proxy UUID in a profile's `proxy` field: `proxy not found:`). |
| `no_permission`     | The API token (or its folder scope) does not allow this action. See [API Token Permissions](authentication.md#api-token-permissions). |
| `validation_error`  | Semantic validation failed (business envelope form, e.g. mac `os_version` not allowed for the platform). Not to be confused with the `validation_error` object of the validation envelope. |
| `limit_reached`     | Resource limit reached on the current subscription. |
| `already_exists`    | Conflict — a record with the same key already exists. |
| `internal_error`    | Server-side fault. Retry. |
| `unknown_error`     | Unclassified failure (from the OpenAPI spec's `ErrorCode` enum). |
| `no_tokens`         | No API token exists for the workspace (from the OpenAPI spec's `ErrorCode` enum). |
| `rate_limit_exceeded` | RPM/RPH bucket empty. See [rate-limiting.md](rate-limiting.md). |

### Profiles

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `profiles.started`               | Profile is already running (`409`, e.g. `POST /profiles/{uuid}/import_cookies` on a running profile). |
| `profiles.not_started`           | Profile is not running (`409`, e.g. `POST /profiles/{uuid}/force_stop` on a stopped profile: `"Profile is not started"`). |
| `profiles.access_error`          | `DELETE /profiles`: none of the requested profiles is accessible to the token (`403`). |
| `profiles.maximum_saved_error`   | `POST /profiles/trash_bin/restore` would exceed the plan's profile limit; nothing is restored (`403`). |
| `profiles.restore_error`         | `POST /profiles/trash_bin/restore` restored nothing (`400`, `"No profiles to restore"`). `data` carries `restored_uuids`, `payment_required_uuids`, `not_found_uuids`. |
| `profiles.stop_error`            | Bulk force-stop stopped none of the profiles (`400`). `data.failed` lists the offending UUIDs. |
| `profiles.consistency_error`     | `version` passed to `force_stop` does not match the server-side version. |
| `profiles.update_error`          | Update payload was rejected, e.g. `fingerprint.os` on `PATCH /profiles/{uuid}` (`You can't update os.`). |
| `profiles.password_error`        | Password set/clear failed (wrong `old_password`/`password`, or a listed profile is running on another machine); nothing is changed. |
| `profiles.invalid_cookie`        | Cookies field is not in JSON, Mozilla, or Netscape format. |
| `profiles.transfer_error`        | Generic transfer failure. |
| `profiles.transfer_no_receiver`  | `receiver_email` is not a member of the workspace. |
| `profiles.transfer_no_profiles`  | None of the supplied UUIDs are eligible for transfer. |
| `profiles.export_error`          | Export operation failed. |
| `profiles.export_limit_exceeded` | Export rate or volume limit reached. |
| `profiles.import_error`          | Import operation failed. |
| `profiles.import_limit_exceeded` | Import rate or volume limit reached. |
| `profiles.import_no_valid_profiles` | None of the supplied export blobs decoded into valid profiles. |

### Other Resources

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `fingerprints.invalid`            | Fingerprint object failed server-side validation. |
| `fingerprints.invalid_mobile_model` | `device_model` is unknown, or the chosen `os_version` is not in that model's `os_versions` list. |
| `fingerprints.invalid_mobile_type` | Android `fingerprint.device_type` is not valid or does not match the chosen `device_model` (`400`, `"invalid mobile type"`). |
| `subscriptions.inactive`          | Workspace has no active subscription. |
| `proxy_providers.empty_balance`   | No traffic left for this provider (`400`, `POST /proxy_providers/proxies`). |
| `proxy_providers.not_exists`      | Unknown or unavailable proxy provider UUID (`400`, not 404; `"Proxy provider is invalid, or not available"`). |
| `proxy_providers.invalid`         | The provider does not offer the requested proxy kind (`400`, same `msg` as above). |
| `proxy.vpn_field_not_applicable`  | `PATCH /proxies/{uuid}` on a VPN proxy with connection fields such as `host` or `login` (`400`, `"Connection fields cannot be set on a VPN proxy"`). |
| `proxy.limit_reached`             | The plan limit of provider proxies is reached (`403`, `POST /proxy_providers/proxies`; per the official Postman collection). |
| `proxy.maximum_saved_error`       | Proxy quota reached on the subscription. |

## Handling Errors in Code

```python
import time
import requests

def call(method, url, headers, max_retries=3, **kwargs):
    for attempt in range(max_retries):
        response = requests.request(method, url, headers=headers, **kwargs)

        if response.status_code == 429:
            time.sleep(int(response.headers.get("Retry-After", "1")))
            continue

        if response.status_code >= 500:
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
            continue

        body = response.json()
        if response.ok and body.get("success"):
            return body

        # Validation envelope? (the business envelope can also carry code "validation_error")
        if isinstance(body.get("validation_error"), dict):
            raise ValueError(f"Validation failed: {body['validation_error']}")

        # Business error
        code = body.get("code")
        msg  = body.get("msg")
        if code == "profiles.started":
            raise RuntimeError("Profile is running — stop it first.")
        if code == "limit_reached":
            raise RuntimeError("Subscription limit reached.")
        raise RuntimeError(f"{response.status_code} {code}: {msg}")

    raise RuntimeError("Exhausted retries")
```

## Debugging Tips

- Log `x-trace-id` from the response headers — Octo Browser support uses it to look up the call server-side.
- For 400s, inspect the `validation_error` object first; it pinpoints the offending field with `loc`. Don't retry a 400 unchanged — it costs extra rate-limit points.
- For 429s, slow your request rate before retrying; never tight-loop on `Retry-After: 0` if the body still says you are rate-limited.
- For 5xx, retry with exponential backoff. If the failure persists, file a support ticket including the trace id.

---

# File: api/profiles.md

# Profiles API

Browser profiles bundle a fingerprint, an optional proxy, browser storage settings and metadata. Profiles are identified by 32-character hex `uuid` strings.

All endpoints return the standard envelope `{ "success": bool, "msg": string, "data": ..., "code": string | null }`. The list endpoints `GET /profiles` and `GET /profiles/trash_bin` additionally return top-level `total_count` and `page`; `GET /profiles/export` nests its pagination inside `data` (see [List Exports](#list-exports)).

Most endpoints need a specific API token permission (Octo 3.2+), noted as **Required permission** under each endpoint; a call without it fails with `403` `no_permission` (see [API Token Permissions](authentication.md#api-token-permissions)). Endpoints without a **Required permission** line (e.g. `GET /profiles`, `GET /profiles/{uuid}`) need no specific permission, but their results are limited to what the token can see.

## Get Profiles

**Endpoint**: `GET /profiles`

Only profiles visible to the API token are returned. Without the Edit profiles permission, `description` is returned masked as `**`.

**Query Parameters**:

| Param         | Type    | Notes |
|---------------|---------|-------|
| `page_len`    | int     | Page size; one of `10, 25, 50, 100`. Default `10`. |
| `page`        | int     | Zero-based page number. Default `0`. |
| `fields`      | string  | Comma-separated list of fields to include in each item. Allowed: `title`, `description`, `proxy`, `start_pages`, `tags`, `status`, `last_active`, `version`, `storage_options`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `has_user_password`, `pinned_tag`, `folder`, `launch_args`, `images_load_limit`, `local_cache`, `extra_info`. Without this parameter only `uuid` is returned. |
| `ordering`    | string  | One of `created`, `-created`, `active`, `-active`, `title`, `-title`. Default `-created`. |
| `search`      | string  | Filter profiles whose title starts with the given string. |
| `search_tags` | string  | Comma-separated list of tag **names**. A profile is returned only when it has **all** of the listed tags. |
| `status`      | int     | Filter by status: `0` not running, `1` running, `2` error. |
| `password`    | bool    | `true` returns only profiles with passwords; `false` returns only profiles without; omit for all. |
| `proxies`     | string  | Comma-separated list of proxy UUIDs, or the special token `@no-proxies-filter` to return only profiles without a proxy. |
| `origin_platforms` | string[] | Filter by profile origin: `desktop`, `android`, `ios` (per the official spec; parameter encoding not verified). |

```bash
curl -X GET "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles?page_len=100&page=0&fields=title,description,folder,proxy,start_pages,tags,status,last_active,version,storage_options,created_at,updated_at&ordering=active" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": [
    { "uuid": "4bbdc824762342f485bed4968533b28a" },
    { "uuid": "4565940d5b9b41f99341fae6f5f3d855" }
  ],
  "total_count": 25,
  "page": 0,
  "code": null
}
```

## Get Profile

Fetch a single profile with the full nested fingerprint. The full object is always returned — a `fields` query parameter is ignored here. `folder` is `null` when the profile is not in a folder. `status` is `0` not running, `1` running, `2` error. The official Postman sample also shows a `user_agent_changed_by_user` field inside `fingerprint`; it was not returned by the live API on 2026-11-18.

The response has one of three shapes depending on the profile's platform: desktop (below), Android (the `fingerprint` carries `device_type`/`device_model` and no `screen`, `cpu`, `ram`, `renderer`, `fonts`, `noise` or `media_devices`; the profile has no `extensions` field — see [fingerprint.md](fingerprint.md#mobile-fields)), or iOS (see [iOS Profiles](#ios-profiles)). `media_devices` is always returned in the flat form, whichever input form was used.

**Endpoint**: `GET /profiles/{uuid}`

```bash
curl -X GET "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/cfd673b04de3433caca327836ae69d19" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": {
    "uuid": "cfd673b04de3433caca327836ae69d19",
    "title": "Quick befitting-sick",
    "description": "",
    "start_pages": [],
    "bookmarks": [],
    "tags": [],
    "pinned_tag": null,
    "folder": null,
    "proxy": null,
    "status": 0,
    "version": "0",
    "storage_options": {
      "cookies": true, "passwords": true, "extensions": true,
      "localstorage": false, "history": false, "bookmarks": true, "serviceworkers": false
    },
    "last_active": null,
    "fingerprint": {
      "os": "win", "os_version": "11", "os_arch": "x86",
      "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ...",
      "screen": "1440x900 @1 SDR",
      "renderer": "NVIDIA GeForce GT 710",
      "languages": { "type": "ip", "data": null },
      "timezone":  { "type": "ip", "data": null },
      "geolocation": { "type": "ip", "data": null },
      "webrtc": { "type": "ip", "data": null },
      "noise": { "webgl": false, "canvas": false, "audio": false, "client_rects": false },
      "media_devices": { "video_in": 1, "audio_in": 1, "audio_out": 1 },
      "fonts": ["Arial", "Times New Roman", "..."],
      "cpu": 12, "ram": 16, "dns": null
    },
    "image": "55e228c7227946b3889f370b54be26c1",
    "extensions": [],
    "launch_args": [],
    "images_load_limit": null,
    "local_cache": false,
    "extra_info": null,
    "has_user_password": true,
    "password_set_at": "2024-08-21T15:41:11",
    "created_at": "2024-08-21T15:40:15",
    "updated_at": "2024-08-21T15:41:11"
  },
  "code": null
}
```

Dates are ISO 8601 in UTC without a timezone suffix. A saved proxy in `proxy` carries `uuid`, `type`, `host`, `port`, `login`, `password`, `change_ip_url`, `external_id`, `vpn_protocol`, `syn_mode`, `title` and `profiles_count` (per the official spec); a temporary proxy has the same fields with `"uuid": ""` and no `title`/`profiles_count`. For a VPN proxy `type` is `"vpn"` and `host`/`port` come from the config's `Endpoint`; the config itself (`conf`) is not returned here:

```json
{
  "uuid": "",
  "type": "vpn",
  "host": "203.0.113.10",
  "port": 51820,
  "login": "",
  "password": "",
  "change_ip_url": null,
  "external_id": null,
  "vpn_protocol": "wireguard",
  "syn_mode": "profile_based"
}
```

### iOS Profiles

Profiles created in the Octo iOS app can be listed and read through the API, but not created: `fingerprint.os` accepts only `win`, `mac` and `android` (`"ios"` is rejected with `400`). Per the official spec, an iOS profile has no `extensions`, and its `fingerprint` is a different object:

| Field           | Type   | Notes |
|-----------------|--------|-------|
| `model`         | string | Device model. |
| `user_agent`    | string | |
| `languages`     | object | `{ "type": "ip" }` or `{ "type": "manual", "value": ["en-US", ...] }`. |
| `locale`        | object | `{ "type": "ip" }` or `{ "type": "manual", "value": "en-US" }`. |
| `webrtc_policy` | enum   | `blocked`, `realIP`, `proxyIP`. |
| `geolocation`   | object | `{ "type": "auto" }`, `{ "type": "real" }`, or `{ "type": "manual", "latitude": "...", "longitude": "...", "accuracy": "..." }` (string values). |

## Create Profile

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles`

**Required permission:** Create profiles. Sending `password` also requires Profile passwords.

> If you omit a parameter, the server generates a sensible value for it. Only override what you specifically need to control.

> Tip: if you are unsure what a working payload looks like, configure a profile in the browser UI, then fetch it with [`GET /profiles/{uuid}`](#get-profile) and reuse the returned fields.

**Request Body** — top-level fields:

| Field             | Type     | Required | Notes |
|-------------------|----------|----------|-------|
| `title`           | string   | yes      | 1–90 characters. |
| `fingerprint`     | object   | yes      | See [fingerprint.md](fingerprint.md). Only `os` is mandatory inside it. With manual `timezone` data you currently have to account for daylight-saving time yourself (upstream caveat). |
| `description`     | string   | no       | Up to 1024 characters. |
| `start_pages`     | string[] | no       | Up to 20 URLs (each ≤ 2048 chars). |
| `bookmarks`       | object[] | no       | Up to 100 `{name, url}` items. |
| `tags`            | string[] | no       | Tag **names** to attach (each 1–20 chars). Tags are referenced by name here, not by UUID. Unknown names are silently ignored. |
| `pinned_tag`      | string   | no       | Tag **name** rendered prominently in the UI. Added to `tags` if missing; an unknown name is ignored. |
| `folder`          | string   | no       | Folder UUID or name to place the profile in (see [folders.md](folders.md)). Octo 3.0+. The folder must be available to the token, otherwise `403` `no_permission`. |
| `password`        | string   | no       | Profile password (4–255 chars). Also requires the Profile passwords permission. |
| `proxy`           | object \| string \| null | no       | Saved proxy by UUID, inline temporary proxy, inline VPN, or `null`. See [Proxy Field](#proxy-field). |
| `storage_options` | object   | no       | Toggles for cookies, passwords, extensions, localstorage, history, bookmarks, serviceworkers. |
| `cookies`         | array \| string | no | JSON array, or a string in JSON, Mozilla, or Netscape format (see below). The string may be base64-encoded; string form is capped at 16 MiB. |
| `image`           | string   | no       | Profile avatar UUID, as in the `image` field of a profile. An unknown UUID falls back to the default image. |
| `extensions`      | string[] | no       | Extensions as `<id>@<version>`, exactly as the `uuid` field of [`GET /teams/extensions`](teams.md). |
| `launch_args`     | string[] | no       | Extra Chromium command-line flags. |
| `images_load_limit` | int \| null | no  | Image size limit in bytes (0–102400000); `null` disables the limit. |
| `local_cache`     | bool     | no       | Persist HTTP cache between sessions. |
| `extra_info`      | object   | no       | Arbitrary JSON **object**, accessible from extensions via `chrome.cookies.getOctoProfileExtraInfo`. Any other JSON type is rejected with `400` (`Value error, should be JSON-object`), although the official spec types it as a string. |

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Test profile from api",
    "description": "test description",
    "start_pages": ["https://fb.com"],
    "tags": ["octo"],
    "pinned_tag": "octo",
    "launch_args": ["--start-maximized"],
    "proxy": {
      "type": "socks5",
      "host": "1.1.1.1",
      "port": 5555,
      "login": "",
      "password": ""
    },
    "storage_options": {
      "cookies": true, "passwords": true, "extensions": true,
      "localstorage": false, "history": false, "bookmarks": true
    },
    "fingerprint": {
      "os": "mac",
      "os_version": "14",
      "os_arch": "x86",
      "renderer": "AMD Radeon Pro 450",
      "screen": "1920x1080 @1 SDR",
      "languages":  { "type": "ip" },
      "timezone":   { "type": "ip" },
      "geolocation":{ "type": "ip" },
      "webrtc":     { "type": "ip" },
      "cpu": 4,
      "ram": 8
    }
  }'
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": { "uuid": "21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9" },
  "code": null
}
```

### Create Mobile Profile

Mobile profiles pick a `device_model` (see [fingerprint.md](fingerprint.md)); `os_version` must be one of that model's `os_versions`. `device_type` is optional, but when sent it must match the model (`400` `fingerprints.invalid_mobile_type` otherwise). Mobile profiles do not support extensions.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Test mobile profile from api",
    "description": "Mobile profiles do not support extensions",
    "fingerprint": {
      "device_model": "SM-T870",
      "device_type": "tablet",
      "os": "android",
      "os_arch": "arm",
      "os_version": "13"
    }
  }'
```

### Proxy Field

The `proxy` field on create/update accepts four forms:

- `{ "uuid": "<proxy-uuid>" }` — attach a saved proxy from [proxies.md](proxies.md). A plain string, `"proxy": "<proxy-uuid>"`, is accepted and means the same.
- `{ "type": "...", "host": "...", "port": ..., "login": "...", "password": "..." }` — a temporary proxy bound to this profile only. In `GET` responses a temporary proxy appears with `"uuid": ""` and no `title`/`profiles_count`.
- `{ "type": "vpn", "conf": "<base64 WireGuard/AmneziaWG config>", "vpn_protocol": "wireguard", "syn_mode": "profile_based" }` — a temporary VPN proxy bound to this profile only (Octo 3.1+). Only `type` and `conf` are required; `vpn_protocol` defaults to `wireguard` (the only value) and `syn_mode` to `profile_based`. See [VPN Proxies](proxies.md#vpn-proxies) for the config requirements and `syn_mode` values. In `GET` responses it appears with `"uuid": ""`, `host`/`port` taken from the config, and without `conf`; it is not listed by `GET /proxies`.
- `null` — detach the proxy. A temporary proxy is deleted in this case, as it is when the profile is switched from it to a saved proxy.

On `PATCH`, an inline proxy or VPN object updates only the passed fields of the profile's own temporary proxy, or creates one if the profile has none.

Temporary proxies cannot be referenced by UUID. Passing the UUID of a temporary proxy, or an unknown UUID, fails with `404`:

```json
{ "success": false, "msg": "proxy not found:", "data": "", "code": "not_found" }
```

### Cookie Formats

The `cookies` field on create/update accepts either an array or a single string in any of these formats:

**JSON**

```json
[
  {
    "domain": ".google.com",
    "expirationDate": 1639134293.313654,
    "hostOnly": false,
    "httpOnly": false,
    "name": "1P_JAR",
    "path": "/",
    "sameSite": "no_restriction",
    "secure": true,
    "value": "2021-11-10-11"
  }
]
```

**Mozilla**

```json
[
  {
    "Path raw": "/",
    "Samesite raw": "no_restriction",
    "Name raw": "NID",
    "Content raw": "2021-11-10-11",
    "Expires raw": "1639134293",
    "Host raw": "https://.google.com/",
    "This domain only raw": "false",
    "HTTP only raw": "false",
    "Send for raw": "true"
  }
]
```

**Netscape** — tab-separated text, one cookie per line (newline-separated for several cookies):

```
.google.com\tTRUE\t/\tTRUE\t1639134293\t1P_JAR\t2021-11-10-1\t544
```

As a JSON request value:

```json
{
  "title": "Test profile from api with netscape cookies",
  "fingerprint": { "os": "win" },
  "cookies": "some.host\tTRUE\t/\tTRUE\t123\tname\tvalue\nsome2.host\tTRUE\t/\tTRUE\t111\tname2\tvalue2"
}
```

### `extra_info` from Extensions

Add `"permissions": ["cookies"]` to the extension's `manifest.json` and call `chrome.cookies.getOctoProfileExtraInfo` from the extension's service-worker:

```js
chrome.cookies.getOctoProfileExtraInfo((extraInfo) => {
  console.log(extraInfo);
});
```

`extra_info` is delivered to the extension as a JSON string. In the API it must be sent as an object, e.g. `"extra_info": { "any": "value" }`.

## Update Profile

**Endpoint**: `PATCH /profiles/{uuid}`

**Required permission:** Edit profiles.

All fields are optional. The body shape matches `POST /profiles`, except that `password` is not accepted here — use [`POST /profiles/set_password`](#set-profiles-password) instead. A partial `fingerprint` object is accepted (only the listed sub-fields change), but `fingerprint.os` cannot be changed: any `fingerprint` containing `os` — even the current value — is rejected with `400` `profiles.update_error` (`You can't update os.`). `images_load_limit` is accepted here.

Clearing values:
- `tags: []` removes all tags.
- `pinned_tag: null` unpins the tag.
- `folder: null` removes the profile from its folder. A target `folder` must be available to the token, otherwise `403` `no_permission`.
- `proxy: null` detaches the proxy (see [Proxy Field](#proxy-field)).

> Updating running profiles works, but for synchronisation safety prefer to update stopped profiles.

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/d9623a2be9a0431784aacc4500d7963a" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "new title",
    "description": "new description",
    "tags": ["octo"],
    "fingerprint": { "os_version": "11", "screen": "1920x1080 @1 SDR" }
  }'
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": { "uuid": "d9623a2be9a0431784aacc4500d7963a" },
  "code": null
}
```

## Delete Profiles

**Endpoint**: `DELETE /profiles`

**Required permission:** Delete profiles.

**Request Body**:
- `uuids` (string[], required) — profiles to delete, 1–100 per request.
- `skip_trash_bin` (bool, optional, default `true`) — `true` (the default) deletes the profiles permanently; `false` moves them to the trash bin, from where they can be listed with [Get Trash Bin](#get-trash-bin) and returned with [Restore Profiles](#restore-profiles).

The request has a JSON body — make sure your HTTP client sends a body with `DELETE` requests.

```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"uuids":["a4708a63d55742a09b7f1a600c248484","d7226450b9fb4bac8526c24fc3669814","9f0e1d2c3b4a49588776655443322110"], "skip_trash_bin": false}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "Profiles deleted",
  "data": {
    "deleted_uuids":   ["a4708a63d55742a09b7f1a600c248484"],
    "active_uuids":    ["d7226450b9fb4bac8526c24fc3669814"],
    "protected_uuids": [],
    "not_found_uuids": ["9f0e1d2c3b4a49588776655443322110"]
  },
  "code": null
}
```

The response splits the requested UUIDs into four lists:
- `deleted_uuids` — deleted (or moved to the trash bin);
- `active_uuids` — running, not deleted — stop them first and retry;
- `protected_uuids` — protected against deletion through the API (Octo 3.2+), not deleted;
- `not_found_uuids` — not in your team, or not accessible to the token.

A `200` does not mean every profile was deleted: check `deleted_uuids`. If nothing was deleted, the request returns `404` `not_found` ("Profiles not found or active") with the four lists in `data` (live-verified for the all-unknown case):

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "msg": "Profiles not found or active",
  "data": {
    "deleted_uuids": [],
    "active_uuids": [],
    "protected_uuids": [],
    "not_found_uuids": ["9f0e1d2c3b4a49588776655443322110"]
  },
  "code": "not_found"
}
```

If none of the requested profiles is accessible to the token, the request returns `403` `profiles.access_error` (per the official Postman collection).

## Get Trash Bin

List profiles in the team trash bin, newest first.

**Endpoint**: `GET /profiles/trash_bin`

**Required permission:** Delete profiles.

**Query Parameters**:
- `page` (int, optional) — zero-based page number, default `0`.
- `page_len` (int, optional) — one of `10, 25, 50, 100`, default `10`; any other value is rejected with `400`.
- `search` (string, optional) — filter by profile title; must not be empty (`?search=` returns `400` `string_too_short`).

```bash
curl -X GET "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/trash_bin?page=0&page_len=10" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": [
    {
      "uuid": "4bbdc824762342f485bed4968533b28a",
      "title": "Profile 1",
      "deleted_at": "2026-10-27T10:15:00",
      "deleted_by": "API token (API)",
      "by_automation_api": true,
      "restore": { "paid": false, "price": "0", "free_at": null }
    },
    {
      "uuid": "4565940d5b9b41f99341fae6f5f3d855",
      "title": "Profile 2",
      "deleted_at": "2026-10-26T18:40:00",
      "deleted_by": "user@example.com",
      "by_automation_api": false,
      "restore": { "paid": true, "price": "1", "free_at": "2026-10-28T18:40:00" }
    }
  ],
  "code": null,
  "total_count": 2,
  "page": 0
}
```

- `deleted_by` — the email of the member who deleted the profile, or `"<token name> (API)"` when it was deleted with an API token; `by_automation_api` is `true` for profiles deleted through the API.
- `restore` — current restore terms. Each profile can be restored for free a limited number of times per period; after that a restore costs tokens. `paid` is `true` when restoring now costs tokens, `price` is the price in tokens as a decimal string (`"0"` when free), and `free_at` is when the next free restore becomes available (`null` if it is free now).

## Restore Profiles

Restore profiles from the trash bin. Restorable profiles are restored, the rest are skipped.

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles/trash_bin/restore`

**Required permission:** Delete profiles.

**Request Body**:
- `uuids` (string[], required) — 1–100 per request (an empty list is rejected with `400` `too_short`).

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/trash_bin/restore" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"uuids":["4bbdc824762342f485bed4968533b28a","4565940d5b9b41f99341fae6f5f3d855"]}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": {
    "restored_uuids": ["4bbdc824762342f485bed4968533b28a"],
    "payment_required_uuids": ["4565940d5b9b41f99341fae6f5f3d855"],
    "not_found_uuids": []
  },
  "code": null
}
```

- `restored_uuids` — restored.
- `payment_required_uuids` — in the trash bin, but restoring costs tokens (see `restore` in [Get Trash Bin](#get-trash-bin)). Paid restores are not available through the API: these profiles stay in the trash bin; restore them in the Octo Browser client.
- `not_found_uuids` — not in your team's trash bin (including profiles that were deleted permanently).

A `200` does not mean profiles were restored: check `restored_uuids`. When nothing was restored, the request returns `400` `profiles.restore_error` with the three lists in `data`:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "msg": "No profiles to restore",
  "data": {
    "restored_uuids": [],
    "payment_required_uuids": [],
    "not_found_uuids": ["4bbdc824762342f485bed4968533b28a"]
  },
  "code": "profiles.restore_error"
}
```

If restoring would exceed the profile limit of your plan, the request returns `403` `profiles.maximum_saved_error` and nothing is restored (per the official Postman collection). The official spec also declares `207` for a partial restore (not verified).

## Import Cookies

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles/{uuid}/import_cookies`

**Required permission:** Create profiles.

**Request Body**: `{ "cookies": <array or string> }` — accepts the same JSON, Mozilla and Netscape formats described under [Cookie Formats](#cookie-formats). Cookies can also be uploaded as `multipart/form-data` under the `cookies` field. Cookies are applied on the next profile start. The profile must not be running (`409` `profiles.started` otherwise).

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/d9623a2be9a0431784aacc4500d7963a/import_cookies" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cookies":[{"domain":".google.com","name":"1P_JAR","value":"2021-11-10-11","path":"/","secure":true,"httpOnly":false,"hostOnly":false,"sameSite":"no_restriction","expirationDate":1639134293.313654}]}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{ "success": true, "msg": "Cookies imported", "data": "", "code": null }
```

## Force Stop Profile

Marks a running profile as stopped without syncing. **Unsynced changes are lost.**

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles/{uuid}/force_stop`

**Request Body**:
- `version` (int | numeric string | null, required) — running session version for an optimistic concurrency check; a positive integer or a string of digits such as `"1"`. The field must be present; pass `null` to stop the current session without the check. Omitting it (`{}`) returns a `400` validation error (`Field required`), as does a non-numeric string.

Errors: a `version` that does not match the running session returns `409` `profiles.consistency_error`; a profile that is not running returns `409` `{"success":false,"msg":"Profile is not started","data":"","code":"profiles.not_started"}`.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/d9623a2be9a0431784aacc4500d7963a/force_stop" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"version": null}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{ "success": true, "msg": "Profile stopped", "data": "", "code": null }
```

## Mass Force Stop Profile

Stops several profiles in one call. Unlike the single-profile endpoint, this one takes no `version` and performs no consistency check.

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles/force_stop`

**Request Body**:
- `uuids` (string[], required) — 1–100 per request.

**Response**: `data.failed` lists the UUIDs that were not stopped (for example, profiles that were not running). Status codes:

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 200  | All requested profiles were stopped; `success` is `true` and `data.failed` is empty. |
| 207  | Multi-Status — only some were stopped, per the official Postman collection (not live-verified). |
| 400  | None were stopped; `code` is `profiles.stop_error`. |

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/force_stop" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"uuids":["4b8afed25a524f5aa1dc2922279622f8","21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9"]}'
```

### Example Response (400 — none stopped)

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "msg": "Bulk force stop error",
  "code": "profiles.stop_error",
  "data": { "failed": ["4b8afed25a524f5aa1dc2922279622f8", "21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9"] }
}
```

## Transfer Profiles

Move profiles to another account on the same workspace.

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles/transfer`

**Required permission:** Transfer profiles.

**Request Body**:
- `uuids` (string[], required) — 1–100 entries per request.
- `receiver_email` (string, required) — destination account email.
- `transfer_proxy` (bool, required) — transfer the attached proxies along with the profiles.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/transfer" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"uuids":["21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9"], "receiver_email":"team-mate@example.com", "transfer_proxy": true}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{ "success": true, "msg": "Profiles transferred successfully", "data": "", "code": null }
```

A `200` means at least one profile was transferred; the rest are skipped without being listed.

## Export Profiles

Encode profiles into transferable strings.

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles/export`

**Required permission:** Transfer profiles.

> Paid action — costs 0.5 tokens per profile. Up to 100 profiles per request; duplicate UUIDs are silently ignored.

**Request Body**:
- `uuids` (string[], required) — 1–100 per request.
- `export_proxy` (bool, required) — include the attached proxy data in the export blob. Omitting it returns `400` (`Field required`).

No other fields are accepted: an extra field such as `app_version` is rejected with `400` `extra_forbidden`.

A `200` does not mean every profile was exported: check `exported` and `failed`. The official spec also declares `207` for a partial export and `400` when nothing was exported (not verified).

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/export" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"uuids":["21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9"], "export_proxy": false}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "Profiles exported successfully",
  "data": {
    "exported": [
      {
        "uuid": "21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9",
        "title": "Test profile from api",
        "data": "MEYCIQDcEhji9E69bcOC1853v0zlXIP8kq6ecKwdcejBYkagrwIhAPUU/65bZqoT74AiqKT4IVuKK26zkBN2M9HTFJoZC4rS"
      }
    ],
    "failed": []
  },
  "code": null
}
```

## List Exports

Paginated list of previously generated exports for the account.

**Endpoint**: `GET /profiles/export`

**Required permission:** Transfer profiles.

**Query Parameters**:
- `page` (int, optional) — zero-based page number, default `0`.
- `page_len` (int, optional) — one of `10, 25, 50, 100`, default `10`.

```bash
curl -X GET "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/export?page=0&page_len=10" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": {
    "data": [
      {
        "uuid": "21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9",
        "title": "Test profile from api",
        "data": "JGFlc19nY20kJFpkbkZ6WWlOTVROejNCRnhwVDBuanZJcWp6a0lLemNvV2VpWXEvLkdETC40WFF1QmdwYnlNampRcTRzZ1JSUmJqWHhKMjNWbnVITUxuL1ZTMTBCT1BmaVZZS0E="
      }
    ],
    "total": 1,
    "page": 0
  },
  "code": null
}
```

> Note: this endpoint wraps its list in a nested object — the items are in `data.data`, and pagination uses `data.total` and `data.page` (not top-level `total_count`/`page`). An empty list is returned as `"data": {"data": [], "total": 0, "page": 0}`.

## Get Export

Fetch a single previously generated export.

**Endpoint**: `GET /profiles/export/{uuid}`

**Required permission:** Transfer profiles.

```bash
curl -X GET "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/export/21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": {
    "uuid": "21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9",
    "title": "Test profile from api",
    "data": "JGFlc19nY20kJDMvMzBKcW12d2tXYi91UlRNL1ZHNFNTZEROYUlKSC5wbDRwWTdkaFlac0pBRUE4dkpVOXVRclhnWnpPT3N5eUtUOUlKOGMveTZkekpmemRPMEFMd3Z0YnBsenM="
  },
  "code": null
}
```

## Import Profiles

Restore profiles from export blobs.

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles/import`

**Required permission:** Create profiles.

> Up to 100 profiles per request.

**Request Body**:
- `data` (array, required) — up to 100 items, each in one of three forms:
  - a string — the `data` blob from [`POST /profiles/export`](#export-profiles);
  - an object `{ "data", "title", "uuid" }` — an entry from a new-format export file, passed verbatim;
  - an object `{ "data": "<json string>", "signature" }` — an entry from an old (V1) export file.
- `folder` (string, optional) — folder UUID or name to place the imported profiles in (see [folders.md](folders.md)). Octo 3.0+. The folder must be available to the token, otherwise `403` `no_permission`.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/import" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data":["MEYCIQDcEhji9E69bcOC1853v0zlXIP8kq6ecKwdcejBYkagrwIhAPUU/65bZqoT74AiqKT4IVuKK26zkBN2M9HTFJoZC4rS"]}'
```

Import from a new-format export file:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "data": "JGFlc19nY20kJE1mUk9tVS5KUGhrZmZyeGVCcGpzQ1VDa2xOUWRtcGdtVXc2WGdnMldqNWU5bFdHcGFnME5LSzZQa1BZLndsdnZEMWRZdHRudG5GdW5xakk5aUxyRWIycHhWdw==",
      "title": "[Imported] Quick bouncy-reception",
      "uuid": "761c6c15b2e44545851061555c665319"
    }
  ]
}
```

Import from an old-format (V1) export file:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "data": "{\"title\": \"[Imported] Quick rosy-chairlift\", \"exported_at\": \"2023-12-06 08:58:38\", \"profile\": \"gAAAAABlcDhTKzTeRIj2pGHBg-zJggNGMsekvt2DT47uM_iZYua9yoEmov0x3ZQKOu-XSWjgMGLL3CAC8rN92zyj-qOBVw3bnA==\"}",
      "signature": "MEUCIQD4ynaphY6R0TjQPz6hb5cmPaN5W+5pguRT65a6KB4r/gIgDOOcLfRvhrmeYHSpRIKSnjaziXM6lrS1OvVm86vxKVk="
    }
  ]
}
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "Profiles imported successfully",
  "data": { "failed": [] },
  "code": null
}
```

## Set Profiles Password

Set or change the password protecting one or more profiles. The same password is applied to every listed profile. The request is all-or-nothing: if `old_password` does not match for one of the profiles, or one of them is currently running on another machine, the whole request fails with `400` and no profile is changed.

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles/set_password`

**Required permission:** Profile passwords.

**Request Body**:
- `profiles` (string[], required) — profile UUIDs.
- `password` (string, required) — new password, 4–255 characters.
- `old_password` (string, required when any listed profile already has a password) — a single value that must match the current password of every listed profile that has one. Omit when none of them has a password yet.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/set_password" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"profiles":["21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9"], "password":"new-pw", "old_password":"old-pw"}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{ "success": true, "msg": "Password has been set for selected profiles", "data": "", "code": null }
```

## Clear Profile Password

Remove the password from a single profile. The current password must be provided; if it does not match, the request fails with `400` `profiles.password_error`.

**Endpoint**: `POST /profiles/{uuid}/clear_password`

**Required permission:** Profile passwords.

**Request Body**:
- `password` (string, required) — current profile password.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles/21d471786f4e4038811e1e78371831d9/clear_password" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"password":"current-pw"}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{ "success": true, "msg": "Password has been cleared", "data": "", "code": null }
```

## Common Errors

- **400 Bad Request** — body fails validation (see the `validation_error` object in [errors.md](errors.md)), an unsupported `os_version` for the platform (envelope with `code: "validation_error"`), a `device_model`/`device_type` mismatch (`fingerprints.invalid_mobile_model`, `fingerprints.invalid_mobile_type`), `fingerprint.os` sent on `PATCH` (`profiles.update_error`), a wrong password (`profiles.password_error`), a mass `force_stop` that stopped nothing (`profiles.stop_error`), or a trash-bin restore that restored nothing (`profiles.restore_error`).
- **403 Forbidden** — the token lacks the required permission or the `folder` is not available to it (`no_permission`), none of the profiles in `DELETE /profiles` is accessible to the token (`profiles.access_error`), or a restore would exceed the plan's profile limit (`profiles.maximum_saved_error`).
- **404 Not Found** — profile UUID does not exist, `DELETE /profiles` deleted nothing (`not_found`, with the four lists in `data`), or the `proxy` UUID is unknown or belongs to a temporary proxy (`proxy not found:`).
- **409 Conflict** — profile is locked, running (`profiles.started`, e.g. on `import_cookies`), not running on `force_stop` (`profiles.not_started`), or its `version` does not match (`profiles.consistency_error`).
- Unknown tag **names** (≤ 20 chars) in `tags[]` are not an error: the request succeeds and the tag is silently dropped (no tag is auto-created). Names longer than 20 characters return `400` `string_too_long`.

---

# File: api/tags.md

# Tags API

Tags are coloured labels attached to browser profiles. They are managed independently and referenced **by name** (1–20 characters) from profile payloads; tag UUIDs are used only by `PATCH /tags/{uuid}` and `DELETE /tags/{uuid}`.

All endpoints return the standard envelope `{ "success": bool, "msg": string, "data": ..., "code": string | null }`.

## Get Tags

List every tag on the account.

**Endpoint**: `GET /tags`

```bash
curl -X GET "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/tags" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": [
    {
      "uuid": "3524ff6e3f0245ffbbcb5ea3d0446a8e",
      "name": "aaaa",
      "color": "grey"
    },
    {
      "uuid": "07fd5038fc0743cd955d963a19edb3d9",
      "name": "facebook",
      "color": "blue"
    },
    {
      "uuid": "ab1391ce01aa46fcbdd9d02a4569bec4",
      "name": "google",
      "color": "yellow"
    },
    {
      "uuid": "7891009afee84952a926b03e7bc0af52",
      "name": "octo",
      "color": "orange"
    }
  ],
  "code": null
}
```

## Create Tag

**Endpoint**: `POST /tags`

**Required permission:** Edit tags.

Returns HTTP `201 Created`.

**Request Body**:
- `name` (string, required) — tag name, 1–20 characters.
- `color` (string, optional) — one of: `grey`, `blue`, `cyan`, `orange`, `green`, `purple`, `red`, `yellow`. Defaults to `grey`. Hex colours are not accepted.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/tags" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"supertag","color":"blue"}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": {
    "uuid": "ab003313e690425cb1f01e67b9b3a5da",
    "name": "supertag",
    "color": "blue"
  },
  "code": null
}
```

## Update Tag

**Endpoint**: `PATCH /tags/{uuid}`

**Required permission:** Edit tags.

Both `name` and `color` are optional; supply only the fields you want to change (e.g. `{"color":"red"}` alone is accepted). `name` is still limited to 1–20 characters. Returns HTTP `200 OK`.

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/tags/ab003313e690425cb1f01e67b9b3a5da" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"supertag1","color":"orange"}'
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": {
    "uuid": "ab003313e690425cb1f01e67b9b3a5da",
    "name": "supertag1",
    "color": "orange"
  },
  "code": null
}
```

## Remove Tag

**Endpoint**: `DELETE /tags/{uuid}`

**Required permission:** Edit tags.

```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/tags/ab003313e690425cb1f01e67b9b3a5da" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": null,
  "code": null
}
```

## Using Tags with Profiles

Profile payloads reference tags **by name** (not by UUID — the UUIDs above are only used for `PATCH /tags/{uuid}` and `DELETE /tags/{uuid}`). The `tags` field on a profile is an array of tag names, and `pinned_tag` is a single tag name:

```json
{
  "title": "My Profile",
  "tags": ["facebook", "google"],
  "fingerprint": { "os": "win" }
}
```

### Search Profiles by Tags

`GET /profiles` accepts `search_tags`, a comma-separated list of tag **names**. A profile is returned only when it has **all** listed tags (logical AND, not OR).

```bash
curl -X GET "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/profiles?page_len=10&page=0&search_tags=facebook,google" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

## Common Errors

- **400 Bad Request** — invalid colour, missing `name` on create, `name` longer than 20 characters (`string_too_long`), or malformed UUID.
- **403 Forbidden** — `no_permission`: the API token lacks the Edit tags permission.
- **404 Not Found** — tag UUID does not exist.
- **409 Conflict** — tag name already exists on the account.

See [errors.md](errors.md) for the standard error envelope and validation-error payload.

---

# File: api/folders.md

# Folders API

Folders group browser profiles for organisation and access control. They were introduced in Octo Browser 3.0 (July 2026) and are managed independently, then referenced from profile payloads via the `folder` field.

All endpoints return the standard envelope `{ "success": bool, "msg": string, "data": ..., "code": string | null }`.

## Get Folders

Returns the folders available to the calling token. A token with restricted folder access gets only its folders, possibly an empty list. The response is not paginated.

**Endpoint**: `GET /folders`

```bash
curl -X GET "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/folders" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": [
    {
      "uuid": "4d867ccd37224526ac2f6a65761c8614",
      "name": "clients",
      "assignable_wo_permission": false
    }
  ],
  "code": null
}
```

## Create Folders

Creates one or more folders in a single request.

**Endpoint**: `POST /folders`

**Required permission:** Edit folders. Setting `assignable_wo_permission` additionally requires Manage team.

Returns HTTP `200 OK` (not `201`, unlike `POST /profiles`, `POST /tags`, and `POST /proxies`).

**Request Body**:
- `folders` (array, required) — 1 to 100 folder objects, each with:
  - `name` (string, required) — folder name, 1–20 characters.
  - `assignable_wo_permission` (bool, optional) — whether profiles can be assigned to this folder without an explicit folder permission. Defaults to `false`.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/folders" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"folders":[{"name":"clients"}]}'
```

### Example Response

`data` is an array of the created folders:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": [
    {
      "uuid": "4d867ccd37224526ac2f6a65761c8614",
      "name": "clients",
      "assignable_wo_permission": false
    }
  ],
  "code": null
}
```

## Update Folder

**Endpoint**: `PATCH /folders/{folder}`

**Required permission:** Edit folders. Setting `assignable_wo_permission` additionally requires Manage team.

The `{folder}` path parameter accepts either the folder UUID or the folder name. Both body fields are optional; supply only what you want to change:
- `name` (string, optional) — new name, 1–20 characters.
- `assignable_wo_permission` (bool, optional).

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/folders/4d867ccd37224526ac2f6a65761c8614" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"clients-eu","assignable_wo_permission":true}'
```

### Example Response

`data` is the updated folder object:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": {
    "uuid": "4d867ccd37224526ac2f6a65761c8614",
    "name": "clients-eu",
    "assignable_wo_permission": true
  },
  "code": null
}
```

## Remove Folder

**Endpoint**: `DELETE /folders/{folder}`

**Required permission:** Edit folders.

The `{folder}` path parameter accepts either the folder UUID or the folder name.

```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/folders/clients-eu" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": null,
  "code": null
}
```

## Using Folders with Profiles

Profile payloads accept an optional `folder` field (string) on `POST /profiles`, `PATCH /profiles/{uuid}`, and `POST /profiles/import` to place the profile into a folder.

## Common Errors

- **400 Bad Request** — validation failure, e.g. a name longer than 20 characters. Note that this payload has no `success`/`msg`/`data`/`code` envelope, only `validation_error`:

  ```json
  {
    "validation_error": {
      "body_params": [
        {
          "type": "string_too_long",
          "loc": ["name"],
          "msg": "String should have at most 20 characters",
          "input": "a-folder-name-that-is-too-long"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
  ```

- **403 Forbidden** — `no_permission`: the API token lacks Edit folders (or Manage team when setting `assignable_wo_permission`), or the folder is not available to the token.

- **404 Not Found** — folder UUID or name does not exist:

  ```json
  {
    "success": false,
    "msg": "Folder not found",
    "data": "",
    "code": "not_found"
  }
  ```

See [errors.md](errors.md) for the standard error envelope.

---

# File: api/proxies.md

# Proxies API

Manage saved proxies. A proxy is a reusable record that can be referenced by UUID from a profile, or supplied inline on a profile payload.

A saved proxy is either a regular proxy (`http`, `https`, `socks`, `socks5`, `ssh`) or a VPN tunnel (`type: "vpn"`) defined by a WireGuard or AmneziaWG (AWG) configuration file (Octo 3.1+). Proxies bought from the providers built into Octo Browser (the Proxy Shop) are managed separately and do not appear in `GET /proxies` — see [proxy-providers.md](proxy-providers.md).

All endpoints return the standard envelope `{ "success": bool, "msg": string, "data": ..., "code": string | null }`.

## Get Proxies

**Endpoint**: `GET /proxies`

Returns all saved proxies as a bare array (no pagination). Every item carries `conf`, `vpn_protocol` and `syn_mode`; on regular proxies they are `null`. On VPN proxies `conf` holds the full base64-encoded configuration, `login` and `password` are `""`, and `host`/`port` are taken from the config's `Endpoint` line.

```bash
curl -X GET "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/proxies" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": [
    {
      "conf": null,
      "uuid": "963d30cb2d7247c89da222c8a9dcab29",
      "type": "socks5",
      "port": 29801,
      "host": "localhost",
      "login": "some_login",
      "password": "some_password",
      "change_ip_url": "https://localhost/api/v1/change-ip?uuid=c26dc4d6-0de7-4aeb-bbef-de3d98362f4e",
      "external_id": null,
      "vpn_protocol": null,
      "syn_mode": null,
      "title": "example proxy",
      "profiles_count": 0
    },
    {
      "conf": "W0ludGVyZmFjZV0KUHJpdmF0ZUtleSA9IEFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUE9CkFkZHJlc3MgPSAxMC4wLjAuMi8zMgoKW1BlZXJdClB1YmxpY0tleSA9IEJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkI9CkFsbG93ZWRJUHMgPSAwLjAuMC4wLzAKRW5kcG9pbnQgPSAxOTIuMC4yLjE6NTE4MjAK",
      "uuid": "23b512d979394d4097c5a6ddf04217b0",
      "type": "vpn",
      "port": 51820,
      "host": "192.0.2.1",
      "login": "",
      "password": "",
      "change_ip_url": null,
      "external_id": null,
      "vpn_protocol": "wireguard",
      "syn_mode": "profile_based",
      "title": "my-vpn-proxy",
      "profiles_count": 0
    }
  ],
  "code": null
}
```

> **Security note**: proxy `login` and `password` are returned in clear text, and a VPN proxy's `conf` decodes to the full WireGuard/AmneziaWG config including the client `PrivateKey`. Avoid logging full responses.

## Create Proxy

**Endpoint**: `POST /proxies`

**Required permission:** Create proxies.

Returns HTTP `201 Created`. Unknown body fields are rejected. The body has two forms, chosen by `type`: the regular form below and the [VPN form](#vpn-proxies). Validation errors name the form in `loc` — `["plain", ...]` for the regular form, `["vpn", ...]` for the VPN form.

**Request Body** (regular form):
- `type` (string, required) — one of `http`, `https`, `socks`, `socks5`, `ssh` (or `vpn` for the VPN form).
- `host` (string, required) — an IPv4/IPv6 address or a hostname of 4–253 characters.
- `port` (integer, required) — 0–65535.
- `title` (string, required) — 1–255 characters.
- `login` (string, optional) — up to 255 characters.
- `password` (string, optional) — up to 255 characters.
- `change_ip_url` (string, optional) — URL hit by the rotate-IP action; a valid URI, 1–65536 characters.
- `external_id` (string, optional) — your own identifier, up to 255 characters; preserved in responses.

**Response**: the created proxy object, including `uuid`, `profiles_count` (number of profiles using the proxy, `0` for a new proxy), and `conf`/`vpn_protocol`/`syn_mode` (`null` for a regular proxy).

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/proxies" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "type": "socks",
    "host": "localhost",
    "port": 1081,
    "login": "user",
    "password": "secret111",
    "title": "super proxy",
    "change_ip_url": "http://example.com",
    "external_id": "12345"
  }'
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": {
    "conf": null,
    "uuid": "789f4d3f898d4e10acf2bebd249fcf95",
    "type": "socks",
    "port": 1081,
    "host": "localhost",
    "login": "user",
    "password": "secret111",
    "change_ip_url": "http://example.com",
    "external_id": "12345",
    "vpn_protocol": null,
    "syn_mode": null,
    "title": "super proxy",
    "profiles_count": 0
  },
  "code": null
}
```

### VPN Proxies

Send `"type": "vpn"` to create a VPN proxy from a WireGuard or AmneziaWG configuration file.

**Request Body** (VPN form):
- `type` (string, required) — `vpn`.
- `title` (string, required) — 1–255 characters.
- `conf` (string, required) — the configuration file, base64-encoded UTF-8 text; up to 16 KB before encoding (at most 21848 characters encoded). It must contain an `Endpoint = host:port` line: the proxy's `host` and `port` are read from it.
- `syn_mode` (string, optional) — the TCP/IP (SYN) fingerprint the tunnel emulates; default `profile_based`. See the table below.
- `vpn_protocol` (string, optional) — `wireguard`, the only accepted value and the default. Use `wireguard` for AmneziaWG configs too.
- `external_id` (string, optional) — your own identifier, up to 255 characters.

`host`, `port`, `login`, `password` and `change_ip_url` are not accepted in the VPN form (`400`, `extra_forbidden`): the endpoint comes from the config, and a tunnel has no credentials or rotation URL. In responses a VPN proxy has `login`/`password` `""` and `change_ip_url` `null`.

`syn_mode` values:

| Value           | Meaning |
|-----------------|---------|
| `profile_based` | Emulate the OS of the profile the proxy is attached to (default). |
| `win`           | Always emulate Windows, whatever the profile's OS. |
| `mac`           | Always emulate macOS, whatever the profile's OS. |
| `android`       | Always emulate Android, whatever the profile's OS. |
| `real`          | Keep the real TCP/IP stack of the machine running the browser. |

Encode the config file as a single base64 line, e.g. `base64 -w0 wg0.conf` (Linux) or `base64 -i wg0.conf` (macOS). The `conf` in the example below decodes to:

```text
[Interface]
PrivateKey = AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=
Address = 10.0.0.2/32

[Peer]
PublicKey = BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB=
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0
Endpoint = 192.0.2.1:51820
```

```bash
curl -X POST "https://app.octobrowser.net/api/v2/automation/proxies" \
  -H "X-Octo-Api-Token: YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "type": "vpn",
    "title": "my-vpn-proxy",
    "conf": "W0ludGVyZmFjZV0KUHJpdmF0ZUtleSA9IEFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUE9CkFkZHJlc3MgPSAxMC4wLjAuMi8zMgoKW1BlZXJdClB1YmxpY0tleSA9IEJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkI9CkFsbG93ZWRJUHMgPSAwLjAuMC4wLzAKRW5kcG9pbnQgPSAxOTIuMC4yLjE6NTE4MjAK",
    "syn_mode": "profile_based"
  }'
```

#### Example Response

The created VPN proxy, with `conf` echoed back:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "data": {
    "conf": "W0ludGVyZmFjZV0KUHJpdmF0ZUtleSA9IEFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUFBQUE9CkFkZHJlc3MgPSAxMC4wLjAuMi8zMgoKW1BlZXJdClB1YmxpY0tleSA9IEJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkJCQkI9CkFsbG93ZWRJUHMgPSAwLjAuMC4wLzAKRW5kcG9pbnQgPSAxOTIuMC4yLjE6NTE4MjAK",
    "uuid": "23b512d979394d4097c5a6ddf04217b0",
    "type": "vpn",
    "port": 51820,
    "host": "192.0.2.1",
    "login": "",
    "password": "",
    "change_ip_url": null,
    "external_id": null,
    "vpn_protocol": "wireguard",
    "syn_mode": "profile_based",
    "title": "my-vpn-proxy",
    "profiles_count": 0
  },
  "code": null
}
```

#### VPN Validation Errors

All are `400` with a `validation_error.body_params` list:

| Problem | `type` / `loc` | `msg` |
|---------|----------------|-------|
| `conf` missing | `missing` / `["vpn","conf"]` | `Field required` |
| `conf` is not base64 | `value_error` / `["vpn","conf"]` | ``Value error, Config must be base64-encoded UTF-8 text`` |
| No `Endpoint` line in the config | `value_error` / `["vpn","conf"]` | ``Value error, Config has no `Endpoint = host:port` `` |
| `vpn_protocol` other than `wireguard` | `enum` / `["vpn","vpn_protocol"]` | `Input should be 'wireguard'` |
| Unknown `syn_mode` | `enum` / `["vpn","syn_mode"]` | `Input should be 'profile_based', 'win', 'mac', 'android' or 'real'` |
| `host`, `port`, `login`, … sent | `extra_forbidden` / `["vpn","host"]` | `Extra inputs are not permitted` |

```json
{
  "validation_error": {
    "body_params": [
      {
        "type": "extra_forbidden",
        "loc": ["vpn", "host"],
        "msg": "Extra inputs are not permitted",
        "input": "192.0.2.10"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Update Proxy

**Endpoint**: `PATCH /proxies/{uuid}`

**Required permission:** Edit proxies.

All body fields are optional; supply only the fields you want to change. Unknown fields are rejected. As with create, the body has a regular and a VPN form.

**Request Body** (regular form):
- `type` (string) — `http`, `https`, `socks`, `socks5`, `ssh`; or `vpn` to convert the proxy into a VPN proxy (then use the VPN form).
- `title` (string) — 1–255 characters.
- `host` (string) — IPv4/IPv6 address or hostname.
- `port` (integer) — 0–65535.
- `login`, `password` (string) — up to 255 characters each; per upstream, an empty string clears the value (not live-verified).
- `change_ip_url` (string).
- `external_id` (string) — up to 255 characters.

**Request Body** (VPN form):
